ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening by a FINTRAC-regulated corporate services provider or Quebec legal counsel. Screening covers: (1) Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act (S.C. 1992, c.17), and all UNSC sanctions implemented by the United Nations Act (S.C. 2021, c.9); (2) global PEP databases at 0.95 weighted match threshold; (3) OFAC SDN and UK OFSI lists on a best-practice basis because USDC and USD clearing may touch U.S. financial infrastructure; (4) Quebec Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) enforcement and licensing records under the Quebec Securities Act (CQLR c. V-1.1). Any positive hit requires escalation to the AML compliance officer and a written go/no-go consent before filing of the LP registration.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online name reservation and business registry portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, s. 39, the enterprise name must be in French. A non-French name is accepted only where it is a registered trademark within the meaning of the Trademarks Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. T-13) and no generally known French version exists. For non-Latin-script names, the REQ requires a romanized or transliterated rendering, accompanied by a declaration that it is a transliteration; the French version must dominate if the name is bilingual.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms implying government or royal patronage: 'Royal', 'Reine', 'Crown', 'Ministère', 'Gendarmerie'
Terms implying regulated financial services: 'Bank', 'Banque', 'Insurance', 'Assurance', 'Trust', 'Fiducie', 'Financière' — prior authorization from Quebec AMF or OSFI is required
Terms suggesting false affiliation with a territory or government: 'Canada', 'Québec', 'Montréal', 'Canadian', 'Mountie'
Terms implying a regulated profession: 'Lawyer', 'Avocat', 'Notary', 'Notaire', 'Engineer', 'Ingénieur' unless the holder of a permit from the competent professional body
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the REQ refuses a name, the applicant may submit a written request for administrative review to the Registraire des entreprises within 30 days of the refusal, setting out legal arguments and any corrected name. The registrar must decide within 15 days of receiving the review. A second refusal may be appealed to the Court of Québec (Administrative and Appeal Division) within 30 days of the refusal decision. No formal extension of a reserved name is available; the applicant may instead file a fresh reservation application after the 90-day window or while an appeal is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible on a restricted basis. The limited partnership must maintain a real, geolocatable street address in Quebec for the registered office; a post office box is not accepted. A commercial virtual office with dedicated suite, reception desk, mail handling, and service-of-process capability is generally acceptable. For the ISIC 7110 virtual concert metaverse business, substance is evidenced by contractual production facilities, administrative functions, online event infrastructure, and the acceptance of USDC and Stripe proceeds through a Quebec-registered payment compliance framework.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 10% probability of an unannounced physical inspection in the first 24 months for this low-risk virtual-event entity; 35% if the entity adds regulated ticketing, tokenization, or fiat payment processing at scale; documentary verification requests remain a 20% annual risk.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec, arts. 2236–2260 (limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-45), ss. 1, 15, 19, 24, 25 (registration obligations)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), Revenu Québec
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite (Declaration of Registration for a Limited Partnership)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; capital contributions are set in the partnership agreement. No escrow account requirement under Quebec law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the limited partnership be and hereby is formed under the Civil Code of Quebec and that the General Partner be and hereby is authorized to execute and file the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the limited partnership be established at [address in Quebec], and the first general partner be appointed to manage the affairs; RESOLVED, that the limited partners' subscriptions as set forth in the partnership agreement be accepted; RESOLVED, that the founding partners be authorized to open bank accounts, appoint service providers, and take any ancillary actions to implement the formation and registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online name reservation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search via REQ's online name reservation service. Select a distinctive legal name ending in 'société en commandite' or 'L.P.' and verify against the Quebec enterprise register and NUANS search. Upon clearance, reserve the name for the statutory period and obtain the name reservation certificate.
required_dossiers: Proposed legal name and name type declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried, respond to REQ within 15 days with clarifications or alternate names; administrative correction is available under Art. 32 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting the Partnership Agreement and Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel or notary in Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a written partnership agreement setting out the general partner, limited partners, capital contributions, profit and loss allocation, transfer and withdrawal rights, and dissolution events. If real property is contributed, notarization is mandatory; otherwise a private written agreement is valid. The declaration of limited partnership must contain the statutory particulars prescribed by the Civil Code and the legal publicity legislation.
required_dossiers: Consent of all partners to the formation
Statement of contributions and liability limitations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defects in the partnership agreement may be cured by a supplementary partner resolution; if notarization is required and omitted, the declaration may be re-executed before a notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing the Declaration of Registration with REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Declaration of Registration for the limited partnership with REQ online or by counter. Include the reserved name, registered office in Quebec, identity of the general partner, number of limited partners, and details of the partnership's activity. Pay the requisite publication fee. Registration perfects the existence of the limited partnership and provides public notice.
required_dossiers: Form: Déclaration d'immatriculation – Société en commandite
Valid identification for general and limited partners
Proof of registered office address in Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a query or correction notice, submit the requested amendments or additional documents within the prescribed period; failure to cure may require re-filing and payment of additional fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Regulatory Registrations (Quebec and Federal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After REQ registration, register the limited partnership for Quebec GST/QST and any required provincial or federal accounts. Obtain a Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and the CRA business number (BN). If hiring employees, register with CNESST and CRA payroll accounts. For digital ticketing and USDC payments, no special payment licence is required in Quebec, but FINTRAC AML obligations apply to certain money-services activities.
required_dossiers: Partnership agreement and legal name certificate
General partner identification and corporate authorization, if applicable
Bank account details and KYC documents for financial institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, request reactivation or amendment through Revenu Québec's online portal; disputes over account registration may be resolved by administrative reconsideration or objection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no physical industrial establishment is required for virtual concert hosting and digital ticketing. If a physical office, studio, or data centre is later used, municipal building and zoning permits may apply.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable (no statutory operating or manufacturing licence for virtual event hosting in Quebec).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no physical project, construction, or discharge is involved; full EIA and REAFIE authorization are not required under the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c. Q-2).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable. Cloud-based operations produce no wastewater, VOC, or stack emissions. Any incidental equipment use must comply with municipal noise by-laws and Canadian electronic waste disposal and recycling standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for a purely virtual operation. If a physical office or studio is opened, obtain fire safety inspection and clearance from the municipal fire prevention service and occupational health and safety compliance clearance from CNESST.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA/ARC); federal portal: canada.ca/en/revenue-agency (Business Registration Online and My Business Account). Provincial counterpart for Quebec: Revenu Québec at revenuquebec.ca; partnership registry: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign limited partnership (CA_LP): (1) obtain a federal Business Number (BN) via Form RC1 with the GST/HST program account (RT) through CRA's Business Registration Online, identifying each partner and the partnership; (2) register the extra-provincial LP with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), obtaining the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and filing the required partnership declaration; (3) use the NEQ to open the QST account (RM) with Revenu Québec, plus QPIP and CNESST accounts if payroll is created; (4) mandatory registration arises when taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a calendar quarter or over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; voluntary registration is available below the threshold and is necessary to claim input tax credits on platform and streaming costs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: For income tax purposes the LP is fiscally transparent; income, losses, and tax credits flow through to general and limited partners, and non-resident partners remain assessable under Part I of the Income Tax Act on Canadian-source partnership business income. For GST/HST and QST purposes, however, the partnership itself is a separate person and must register and report in its own name; partners are jointly and severally liable for the LP's GST/HST obligations to the extent provided by the Excise Tax Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no United States-style check-the-box election. Available elections include: the Excise Tax Act s. 273 designated-member election, allowing the LP to designate a partner to file and remit GST/HST for the partnership; the Income Tax Act s. 96(3) election to compute partnership income as if the partnership were a separate person; the ITA s. 97(2) election for a tax-deferred rollover of property into the LP; and the Quebec QST joint-election for members of a closely related group. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are constrained by the ITA's foreign affiliate, FAPI, and specific anti-avoidance provisions rather than by an elective classification regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST — federal value-added tax (5%) plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST, 9.975%); combined headline rate 14.975%. Virtual concert access and digital ticket tokenization constitute taxable supplies of intangible personal property in Canada unless zero-rated as exports.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000: GST small-supplier threshold under ETA s. 240(2); the Quebec QST threshold is harmonized at CAD 30,000. A non-resident LP exceeds the threshold where its taxable supplies, including zero-rated cross-border digital supplies, exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over the four preceding consecutive calendar quarters; Quebec deemed-supply rules may also require non-resident digital vendors to register for QST where their taxable sales into Quebec exceed CAD 30,000 in a 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), or digital stamping regime exists federally or in Quebec. Registrants must issue tax invoices satisfying ETA s. 223(a) (supplier identity and GST/HST BN, recipient identity, invoice date, consideration, and tax charged) and retain books and records in Canada or accessible via electronic media. CRA and Revenu Québec accept EDI and API-driven electronic invoicing; Pan-Canadian PEPPOL e-invoicing adoption is voluntary and does not involve government clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of intangible personal property, including virtual concert access, digital tickets, and metaverse admission, made to non-resident recipients under ETA s. 23(1), provided the right to use is not applied in connection with a commercial or taxable activity in Canada. Physical goods must be exported within 60 days to obtain zero-rating. For the CA_LP, sales to recipients whose billing residence and IP geo-location indicate a non-resident and whose use occurs outside Canada qualify; sales to Canadian or Quebec residents are subject to GST at 5% and QST at 9.975%. Input tax credits on costs related to zero-rated sales are claimable only with valid registration and retained export evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA B13/CAED) — mandatory for physical ancillaries exported from Canada; not applicable to pure digital metaverse access, but absence of export proof for goods revokes zero-rating
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill — evidencing movement of tangible merchandise to a foreign destination; for digital ticket tokenization, an electronic service-delivery log is substituted
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 / Stripe payout report — evidencing receipt of consideration from the non-resident purchaser for the zero-rated export
Non-resident status evidence — KYC record, billing address, IP geo-location, and payment card country code establishing consumption outside Canada
Contract or purchase order expressly stating that the virtual access right is delivered to and consumed by a non-resident purchaser outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: On audit, CRA and Revenu Québec require the full export-evidence bundle; missing or conflicting evidence reverses the zero-rating, the combined 14.975% GST/QST becomes payable with prescribed arrears interest, and previously claimed input tax credits are clawed back. False statements or omissions expose the LP to penalties under ETA s. 280 of the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the tax sought, gross-negligence penalties, and accrued interest. Fraudulent zero-rating claims constitute indictable tax evasion under ETA s. 329, subject to criminal fines and imprisonment, and the normal four-year reassessment limitation is suspended for wilful misrepresentation or fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the currency and monetary authority; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as the prudential bank supervisor; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as the AML/ATF regulator; no standalone foreign-exchange control agency exists in Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible under IMF Article VIII for both current and capital account transactions. Canada does not impose exchange controls, approval requirements, or quantitative limits on profit remittance, partnership distributions, or capital repatriation. The principal frictions are regulatory and tax-oriented: non-resident partners of a Quebec limited partnership must provide Canadian/Quebec tax self-certifications and may face Part XIII withholding tax on Canadian-source amounts unless relief is available under an applicable tax treaty. USDC and other virtual currency proceeds may be converted at commercial rates through regulated Canadian money services businesses or chartered banks, but the handling of virtual currency creates FINTRAC registration and record-keeping obligations under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender requirement, mandatory conversion timeline, or minimum conversion ratio for export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained in CAD, USD, or other currencies in accounts held at Canadian authorized banks, subject only to general foreign-currency reporting for amounts above C$10,000 and to FINTRAC transaction reporting. Virtual-currency transactions related to digital ticket tokenization are reportable if they meet threshold criteria, and the commercial invoice narrative should align with ISIC 7110 / NAICS 711310 to facilitate clean bank and customs/routing classification.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium as a primary settlement rail; High as a supporting collection and conversion front-end. A foreign electronic money institution cannot be a direct Lynx or Real-Time Rail participant and cannot provide final CAD settlement in Canada. If it operates as a money services business in Quebec, it must be registered with FINTRAC and compliant with the Retail Payment Activities Act. The recommended architecture is to use a licensed foreign EMI or digital-bank partner exclusively for USDC receipt, ticket checkout, and conversion, with daily sweeps to a Schedule I Canadian chartered bank account that remains the legal settlement apex.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Canadian/Quebec limited partnership with non-resident partners, most Schedule I banks require at least one principal or authorized signatory with physical presence at a Canadian branch during onboarding, or a remote video interview followed by notarized identity verification. A purely digital remote opening without any Canadian nexus is generally rejected when the entity is newly formed, non-resident-owned, or engaged in virtual-currency-related cash flows. The corporate general partner should identify a designated Canadian-based authorized signatory, officer, or registered agent to facilitate interviews and expedite enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank compliance alert on non-resident limited partners and opaque beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Quebec limited partnership declaration from the Registraire des entreprises; executed limited partnership agreement; certificate of good standing for the corporate general partner; full beneficial ownership chain to a natural person; passports and proof of residential address for each individual owner; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds files; tax residency certificates; bank references from existing relationship banks; legal opinion confirming the validity and commercial substance of the CA_LP structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Red flag for USDC / virtual-currency proceeds and fintech-sourced deposits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FINTRAC money services business registration or written exemption analysis; dedicated virtual-currency compliance manual; blockchain wallet screening and know-your-transaction reports; stablecoin conversion workflow; summary of counterparty KYC for the licensed PSP/EMI; designated AML compliance officer; independent independent audit attestation; ticket terms and refund policy evidencing the non-gambling utility nature of the tokenized event.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear commercial purpose: 'virtual concert metaverse' perceived as gambling, lottery, or high-event-risk activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed virtual event playbook; artist and venue licensing agreements; metaverse platform terms; digital ticket token documentation confirming utility rights only; legal opinion confirming no regulated gambling/receipt-of-bet license is required in Quebec; ISIC 7110 and NAICS 711310 classification note; target geography; chargeback and fraud-control policy; projection of ticket sales and settlement flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity cross-border wire pattern and round-tripping capital movement concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Monthly treasury cash-flow model; whitelisted counterparty schedule; event contracts and invoices supporting all disbursements; Canadian GST/QST/HST registration and CRA/Revenu Québec tax correspondence; accounting-firm engagement letter; monthly reconciliation pack; partnership capital-call notices and subscription schedules; evidence that all partner distributions are arm's-length and tax-compliant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections should be routed by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from the non-resident partner's bank to the Quebec LP's CAD or USD settlement account. Beneficiary must be the full CA_LP legal name and address, and the payment narrative must state 'capital contribution to Canadian limited partnership' or 'subscription for limited partnership units'. Where feasible, use the ISO purpose code 'INVC' (inward investment) or 'CAPT' (capital transfer). The bank's enhanced due diligence file must contain the executed subscription agreement, capital call notice, source-of-funds documentation, beneficial ownership form, CRS/CBOTF self-certification, and a confirming legal opinion. For USDC-to-fiat injections, convert through a regulated FINTRAC-registered Canadian money services business or bank treasury desk, with a fiat wire then sent from the regulated entity to the LP operating account, ensuring a clean legal-tender audit trail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use the following clearing rails: (1) USD vendor, platform, or streaming-service settlements via SWIFT MT103 with cover through the bank's US correspondent network and full invoice remittance information; (2) Canadian dollar vendor payments via EFT Batch or Real-Time Rail to domestic beneficiaries; (3) large infrastructure or event-production procurement via irrevocable documentary letters of credit issued in accordance with UCP600 for sight payment; (4) performer and creator royalty distributions via API-hosted mass-payment files to local and international bank accounts; (5) USDC refunds or distribution payouts reversed through the licensed PSP only after conversion to fiat. Each disbursement must carry a unique reference matching the underlying event contract and must remain available for FINTRAC review and external audit.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/CAD deliverable FX forwards with maturity tenors matched to event receipts and vendor payables
USD/CAD non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) to hedge repatriation where the CAD leg is settled domestically
Cross-currency swaps between USD and CAD for long-term venue, metaverse infrastructure, or capital-equipment contracts
Vanilla USD/CAD call and put options to cap conversion losses from volatile ticket-season cash flows
FX swap and rollover contracts for managing temporary liquidity mismatches between capital injections and outbound disbursements
Stablecoin-to-CAD forward conversion contracts executed through regulated Canadian platforms, with a strict prohibition on speculative open virtual-currency positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Declaration annuelle) - legal publicity and registration update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of each anniversary of the enterprise's registration in the Quebec enterprise register; first declaration due after first registration anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest and penalty of CAD 60 to CAD 220 per declaration; three consecutive unfiled annual declarations trigger administrative strike-off (radiation) and loss of legal existence; general partners may be held personally liable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and T5013 slips for each partner
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of the year following the calendar year-end; for a non-calendar fiscal period, within five months after fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 10 per day per required information return, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 7,500, plus interest; deliberate omissions may trigger gross-negligence penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: TP-600 Partnership Information Declaration (Quebec, when the LP carries on business in Quebec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally the same federal T5013 deadline; for a calendar-year partnership, no later than March 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest, administrative late-filing penalties, loss of tax attestation, and possible prosecution for intentional misrepresentation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No automatic Quebec statutory audit is imposed solely on a limited partnership. An independent audit is mandatory when required by the partnership agreement, lender/investor covenants, securities regulation for a reporting issuer, or when the corporate general partner's own financial statement obligations or governing statute impose an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS for publicly accountable limited partnerships; ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) for private LPs. Tax-basis reporting for the partnership follows the Income Tax Act, Quebec Taxation Act, and Revenu Quebec administrative guidance.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual REQ declaration confirms the current limited and general partners. Quebec transparency rules require the LP to disclose, through the annual declaration or separate UBO register, all individuals with significant control (ISC) holding 25% or more of partnership interests, voting rights, or economic benefits. Any transfer of partnership units must be recorded in the LP's internal register and reflected in the next annual declaration if the ISC changes.
